hook_text: Why do so many African borders run in perfectly straight lines across the desert?
clip_script: Because they were drawn in Europe, with rulers and pencils. That is a result of colonisation. Kings and chiefs lost their power to foreign officials. Borders split the Somali into four pieces and pushed hundreds of peoples into one Nigeria. Colonies were made to send out cocoa, copper, cotton and gold, and buy back factory goods. Railways ran from the mines to the ports, not to the neighbours. Settlers took the White Highlands of Kenya. Mission schools taught reading and Christianity, and English, French and Portuguese became the languages of power. Some things were built, but for whom, paid for by whom, and at what cost? And from those schools came the leaders who won independence.
visual_style: A whiteboard map of Africa with straight border lines being ruled in, railway lines running to the coast with cargo icons, and a mission school with figures that grow into independence leaders.
pacing: Steady, with questions emphasised near the end.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to weigh the results of colonisation.
